summary: After an unpopular vote, a council member moved her daughters to a school two towns away so they would not hear the talk.
realLife: A former mayor and councilwoman said she backed a bill that parents and teachers disliked. To shield her girls from the attention, she moved them to a school two towns over. She told of one daughter overhearing teammates repeat criticism of her mother, and answering it by asking who said it and whether it was believable.
gates: A seat is held and the player has a school-age child in the household.
A vote that a share of the town opposed has passed.
weights: Children at school in the town
Money to pay for a different school
inGame: A held seat, a household with a young child, a school assignment by address, a move changes the school, and a vote the town opposed can carry it.

turns.what: The child shrugs it off and the family stays put.
turns.pulledBy: A sturdy child, a close circle of friends, little press.
turns.writesBack: No move; the child's school tie stays; a small note in the home log.

turns.what: The family keeps the school but a parent drives the child and picks up each day.
turns.pulledBy: Cost of a change, a job that blocks a move.
turns.writesBack: A pickup task on the household's day; less time at work.

turns.what: The child comes home weeks later upset about what a teammate said.
turns.writesBack: A talk scene with the child; the parent's doubt about the seat rises.
